cells.tense: Right now you can set a whole frame on the table and leave it there without treating it as an argument.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Before the week is out, say the shape of one open question plainly, before anyone asks, and then stop talking.
cells.core:
When you know a lot at once, you don't have to make it sound like less. You can carry the full weight of what you see without breaking it into smaller pieces to keep the room comfortable. The frame lands clear, and the room can use it because you said it plainly.

Say the shape of one open question this week — before anyone asks, before you tidy it into something smaller. Say it once and then stop talking. A real shape on the table is worth more to the room than your hedge. If it turns out wrong, it can be corrected, but the missing frame is what people keep tripping over.
cells.sheetLine: You can put the frame on the table before anyone asks.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once
cells.place: under a weight that has to keep being carried

cells.tense: Down the road you are bracing for a choice you can't write in yet, and the bracing has started to cost you the present.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Pick a direction out of the many that are true, walk it for three days, and stop scanning all of them at once.
cells.core:
The fullness starts to turn against you when every true thing becomes something to keep in view at the same time. You are trying to be ready for all the turns at once, and the readiness is eating what it was supposed to protect. The load gets heavier because you won't set any of it down.

Pick one direction out of the many that are true, and walk it for three days. Not forever. Just far enough that your feet know they're on a road. The other true things will still be there when you look, and you'll be steadier for not having held them all up at once.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, and the present is running on a tank you drained.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Say what you see coming to one other person, just to have it out of your own head.
cells.core:
Bearing things alone has pulled you out of the room, and what used to come easily now feels like a draft you keep losing. You don't reach for it because there isn't spare strength to look and hold at once.

Say what you see coming to one other person this week. You don't have to call it a decision; just put it out loud to a person who will hear it. The point isn't to be right. It's to set what you see somewhere it can touch someone else, so the energy comes back into a place that's been running empty.
cells.sheetLine: Say what you see to one other person.

cells.tense: You are already reading the room correctly and then calling it luck, pen down in a room you're writing.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Do the fair thing in a small case where nobody is watching, and don't announce it.
cells.core:
You read a situation and you know what's fair in it, and then some part of you files that under circumstance instead of your own name. When it's going well, that reading is quick and quiet: you simply know, act, and the thing is done with no one told. Nothing needs arguing, and no one has to see.

Do one fair thing this week in a small case where nobody is watching. Do it before you check how it will look, before you decide whether it counts. What you sense about what's right doesn't need a committee. By doing it you find out the reading was yours.
